contentBlocks.text: This week you explored negative numbers four different ways. Let's review it all!

Quick review: negative numbers represent values below zero (Day 1). Further left on a number line means a smaller value (Day 2). Absolute value is distance from zero, always positive (Day 3). You compared real negative numbers in a temperature problem (Day 4). Find |-9|, then order -9, 4, and -2 from least to greatest.
Great work this week — you learned to understand, place, and compare negative numbers, plus absolute value! Next week we'll build on these skills with something new.

objectives: Review negative numbers, number-line placement, absolute value, and real-world comparison
Find an absolute value and order a mixed set of numbers
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child find |-9| and order -9, 4, -2.
3. Complete the review worksheet.
4. Celebrate finishing a full week of real negative-numbers work!
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just the skill the child found hardest this week (often absolute value) rather than requiring all four equally
Ready for more: ask the child to explain the difference between a number's value and its absolute value
This is a good checkpoint to note which of the week's four negative-number skills needs the most reinforcement going forward
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates this week's Common Core Grade 6 negative-numbers standards (6.NS.5/6.NS.6/6.NS.7) before the course continues, matching the established Day-5-review pacing used across every unit this session.
